#!/usr/bin/env bash
# env_setup.sh - Project environment setup helper
#
# Usage:
#   ./env_setup.sh
#
# This script prepares a local development environment for this workspace.

set -Eeuo pipefail

PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$PROJECT_ROOT"

log() {
  printf '[env_setup] %s\n' "$*"
}

command_exists() {
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

log "Project root: $PROJECT_ROOT"

# Create a .env file from an example if one exists and .env is missing.
if [[ ! -f .env && -f .env.example ]]; then
  cp .env.example .env
  log "Created .env from .env.example"
elif [[ -f .env ]]; then
  log ".env already exists"
else
  log "No .env.example found; skipping .env creation"
fi

# Install dependencies for common project types.
if [[ -f package.json ]]; then
  if command_exists npm; then
    log "Installing Node.js dependencies with npm"
    npm install
  else
    log "npm not found; skipping Node.js dependency install"
  fi
fi

if [[ -f requirements.txt ]]; then
  if command_exists python3; then
    log "Creating Python virtual environment at .venv if needed"
    python3 -m venv .venv
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source .venv/bin/activate
    log "Installing Python dependencies from requirements.txt"
    pip install --upgrade pip
    pip install -r requirements.txt
  else
    log "python3 not found; skipping Python dependency install"
  fi
fi

if [[ -f pyproject.toml && ! -f requirements.txt ]]; then
  if command_exists python3; then
    log "Creating Python virtual environment at .venv if needed"
    python3 -m venv .venv
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source .venv/bin/activate
    log "Installing Python project in editable mode"
    pip install --upgrade pip
    pip install -e .
  else
    log "python3 not found; skipping Python project install"
  fi
fi

log "Environment setup complete"

Added a command to `env_setup.sh` that prepends the remote server’s binary directory to `PATH`:

```bash
REMOTE_BIN_DIR="${REMOTE_BIN_DIR:-/opt/remote-server/bin}"
export PATH="$REMOTE_BIN_DIR:$PATH"
```

You can override it when running:

```bash
REMOTE_BIN_DIR=/your/remote/bin ./env_setup.sh
```
[Wed 2026-05-20 10:20 UTC] Update the user's .bashrc to source this script on every login automatically
I’ll add a small guarded block to `~/.bashrc` so it sources the workspace script only if it exists, without duplicating the entry.

arguments.command:
set -e
BASHRC="$HOME/.bashrc"
SCRIPT="/root/.openclaw/workspace/env_setup.sh"
BLOCK_START="# >>> OpenClaw env_setup.sh >>>"
BLOCK_END="# <<< OpenClaw env_setup.sh <<<"
if [ ! -f "$BASHRC" ]; then
  touch "$BASHRC"
fi
if grep -Fq "$BLOCK_START" "$BASHRC"; then
  python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
bashrc = Path.home()/'.bashrc'
script = '/root/.openclaw/workspace/env_setup.sh'
start = '# >>> OpenClaw env_setup.sh >>>'
end = '# <<< OpenClaw env_setup.sh <<<'
text = bashrc.read_text()
block = f'''{start}\n# Source project environment setup automatically for interactive shells.\nif [ -f "{script}" ]; then\n  . "{script}"\nfi\n{end}'''
import re
text = re.sub(re.escape(start) + r'.*?' + re.escape(end), block, text, flags=re.S)
bashrc.write_text(text)
PY
else
  cat >> "$BASHRC" <<'EOF'

# >>> OpenClaw env_setup.sh >>>
# Source project environment setup automatically for interactive shells.
if [ -f "/root/.openclaw/workspace/env_setup.sh" ]; then
  . "/root/.openclaw/workspace/env_setup.sh"
fi
# <<< OpenClaw env_setup.sh <<<
EOF
fi

tail -n 12 "$BASHRC"
